headline: R-TYPE grows a hunter that hunts back
lede: The convoy finally answers fire with pursuit: an armed duelist in the Defender tradition takes the stage on legs 1 and 2 — it tracks your hull across lanes, guns you on a telegraphed clock, and commits to one straight, dodgeable pass. Nothing else on the shelf reacts to you like this.

notes.text: The duelist is live (#2934, PR #2936): authored entries, zero rng. Hunt across lanes on a 110-px stand-off, aimed rounds behind a white-hot eye-glow, then a crouch and one straight dash at tick 260. Two vulcan rounds, a shell ram, a thrown Option or the four-bit orbit fold it for pod money; its body kills at contact.

rtypecheck grew 15 laws (now 216) and two named mutants — pursuit-deaf (the hunter forgets to hunt) and commit-deaf (the duel never ends) — all red-and-named. Winnability floors hold and improved: solo 8/12, co-op 11/12; the README records how the first strafe wiring dropped solo to 2/12 and what guarded it back up.

The autopilot duel is honest: the same lane-field the cabinet shows scores the crouch and the pass, and the pilot walks the lane while a hunter holds the field — but slab commitments outrank the duel, so the brain never trades a wall for a jink.
A QA polish pass (#2938) files what is still short of the original: a distinct crimson round, a phone-scale telegraph, and the slab-overlap read.
